daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo defended his economic views and issued a warning about paid demonstrations during a visit to Gorontalo. Prabowo claimed no economics professors have been able to refute his arguments, while separately warning that he knows who is paying for demonstrations. The president also used a football analogy to describe his role in achieving food self-sufficiency, saying he is the manager operating from outside the field. During the same visit, Sherly Tjoanda received a hero's welcome in Gorontalo, which Prabowo compared to winning a Piala Citra award.

  • Vice President Gibran faced demands for clarification after a UBK student's surprising admission about receiving Rp 20 million sparked controversy, though Gerindra faction defended Gibran over the matter.
  • Gerindra party warned against allowing issues to divide President Prabowo and Vice President Gibran.
  • The KPK is considering forcibly summoning a model who allegedly received Rp 2 billion from a DPR member.
  • The KPK intensely questioned Hilman Latief about parties who initiated the distribution of additional hajj quotas, while the former Director General of PHU shook his head when asked about collusion in the hajj quota case.
  • President Prabowo allowed the public to choose Indonesia's 81st independence anniversary logo.
  • A DPR member proposed that state universities reserve special quotas for students from disadvantaged, frontier, and outermost (3T) regions.
  • The Ombudsman issued 203 recommendations to improve public services.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia is leveraging its membership in international forums to advance Middle East peace efforts. The Foreign Ministry stated that Indonesia uses BRICS and global forums to push for peace in the Middle East. The ministry also emphasized strengthening dialogue to address complaints from Chinese businesspeople operating in Indonesia.

  • Indonesia and South Korea are seeking closer counterterrorism partnership, deepening bilateral security cooperation.
  • Indonesia and Russia signed a new agreement to deepen legal cooperation between the two countries.
  • An Indonesian envoy underscored three priorities for building an ASEAN vaccine ecosystem at a regional meeting.
  • The Defence Ministry stated that health checks were conducted on prospective Kopdes Merah Putih managers before military training, following the death of a TB patient during the training and calls by a UGM expert to evaluate the KDMP military training programme after two SPPI participants died.
  • Indonesian authorities foiled drug smuggling destined for Bali.

Other

The government responded to concerns about Indonesia's potential downgrade by MSCI and a decline in the country's global competitiveness ranking. Officials addressed MSCI's warning that Indonesia could be downgraded to frontier market status, while separately the government is investigating the causes of Indonesia's drop to 48th place in global competitiveness rankings. Coordinating Minister Airlangga stated that Indonesia remains a safe haven for investment amid global turmoil, while a minister highlighted that data centers are key to driving 8 percent economic growth.

  • The government approved a 40-year subsidized mortgage scheme to expand home ownership access.
  • E-commerce platforms must announce fee increases at least 90 days in advance under new regulations.
  • Pertamina recorded positive performance in 2025 with revenue reaching Rp 1,167 trillion.
  • The Attorney General's Office revealed 12 high-value cases including corruption involving tin, Pertamina, and MBG, and claimed to have saved Rp 131.5 trillion over the past six years, though the Attorney General described Benny Tjokro as very skilled at protecting assets from seizure and complained about minimal budgets for maintaining seized assets.
  • Indonesia and the UK agreed to boost funding for biodiversity and conservation projects, while a mining company opened a biodiversity conservation zone in Sulawesi.
  • BPOM announced support for health tourism through special access to herbal medicines, while authorities noted that many pharmaceutical raw materials including paracetamol are still imported.
